explanation: Feet are treated as the least pure part of the body in Hindu-influenced Indian culture, reflected in the widespread custom of charan sparsh — younger people touching an elder's or guru's feet to receive a blessing, which underscores how much spiritual weight is placed on feet. By the same logic, carelessly pointing the soles of your feet at a person, an idol, or religious objects, or touching someone with your foot, reads as disrespectful.
local_tip: Sit with your feet tucked under you or flat on the floor; if you accidentally touch someone or something sacred with your foot, a quick touch of your hand to that person/object followed by touching your own chest is a commonly understood apology gesture.

also_check.note: The feet are considered the lowest part of the body; pointing them at people or sacred objects is a major insult.
Showing the soles of your feet is considered offensive, as feet are seen as unclean.
Generally neutral; putting feet up on furniture may be seen as too casual rather than offensive.
